item.title: Comment on "Beam blow up due to beamstrahlung in circular e+e- colliders"
item.description: arXiv:2610.22453v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The authors of the original article, Valdivia Garcia and Zimmermann (2021), state that they "derive analytical formulae for the equilibrium beam parameters, considering the varying electromagnetic field during the collision". However, to calculate the bending radius in the field of the counter-propagating bunch, they employed an approximation that is completely unjustified. Consequently, a significant portion of the formulae derived in the article bears a very tenuous relationship to reality. For practical purposes, we propose a different solution -- one that is far simpler and more accurate.
item.dc:creator: Dmitry Shatilov

item.title: High average flux positron sources driven by a mJ-class laser
item.description: arXiv:2610.23243v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We report on the production and characterisation of MeV-scale positron populations driven by a high-repetition-rate, mJ-class laser system. The positrons are generated via a two-step Bethe--Heitler process driven by laser-wakefield-accelerated electron beams propagating through a mm-scale lead converter. At 10 Hz, approximately 1000 positrons in the 0.8--1.7 MeV energy range were measured over 100 accumulated shots. Stable electron acceleration was demonstrated at 10 Hz, 100 Hz, and 1 kHz using approximately 9 mJ of laser energy in the focal spot, indicating the potential for substantially higher average positron fluxes for laser systems operating at kHz repetition rates and energies of 10s of mJ. Such a positron source allows generating sufficiently high average fluxes of MeV-scale positrons while maintaining low positron yields per pulse and narrow temporal distributions, a regime of particular interest for novel applications in material science and fundamental physics. The measured positron yields and spectra are in good agreement with Monte Carlo simulations, supporting the modelling of the positron-production process and magnetic transport system.

item.title: Theoretical studies of envelope oscillations and instabilities of mismatched intense charged-particle beams in periodic focusing channels
item.description: arXiv:2401.12171v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The behavior of mismatched intense charged-particle beams in periodic transport channels of the solenoid and quadrupole type is studied theoretically. The envelope-oscillation frequencies of the mismatched beam are obtained by the smooth-approximation method and by numerical evaluation of the linearly perturbed K-V envelope equations. Phase shifts of the envelope oscillations and growth factors per focusing period in the case of instability are calculated for a solenoid and a magnetic quadrupole (FODO) channel using the parameters of the Maryland and GSI beam transport experiments. For comparison and the purpose of illustration, the K-V equations are integrated numerically, and envelope curves as well as single-particle trajectories for mismatched beams are shown in graphical form. In addition, computer simulation studies with the PARMILA code were performed, and results are presented both for K-V and a Gaussian distribution in transverse phase space.\\~\\ Published in: Particle~Accelerators~{\bf 14}, 227--260 (1984)}
item.dc:creator: J\"urgen Struckmeier, Martin Reiser

item.title: On the stability and emittance growth of different particle phase-space distributions in a long magnetic quadrupole channel
item.description: arXiv:2401.12595v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The behavior of K-V, waterbag, parabolic, conical and Gaussian distributions in periodic quadrupole channels is studied by particle simulations. In the parameter range studied, the response associated with the K-V instabilities becomes progressively less pronounced toward the Gaussian distribution. For the third-order instability studied here, the emittance growth factor of an initially Gaussian beam after a large number of periods is considerably lower than that of an equivalent K-V distribution.\newline\indent In addition, the non-K-V distributions exhibit a rapid initial emittance growth within approximately one period of the channel, which becomes very significant at high beam intensities. This growth is attributed to the homogenization of the space-charge density, resulting in a conversion of electric-field energy into transverse kinetic and potential energy. Two simple analytical formulae based on different energy-partition assumptions are derived as estimates for this effect and are compared with the results obtained from particle simulations. They are not rigorous lower and upper bounds for arbitrary beam evolution. \\[6pt] Original publication in Particle Accelerators {\bf 15}, 47--65 (1984)}
item.dc:creator: J\"urgen Struckmeier, J\"urgen Klabunde, Martin Reiser

item.title: Programmable Hard-X-Ray Spectral Comb Generation via Laser-Compton Scattering
item.description: arXiv:2610.17166v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Independent control of line spacing and offset underpins programmable frequency-comb spectroscopy, yet it has not been established for hard-X-ray sources based on inverse Compton scattering after electron transport and angular collection. Self-consistent multi-particle tracking and Li'enard-Wiechert radiation calculations model a transported 10 pC beam and its angle-integrated spectrum near 11 keV. Laser pulse separation programs the comb spacing, while pulse-to-pulse phase translates the entire line grid at fixed spacing. The spacing model agrees within 0.52%, while transport and optics change the phase-transfer slope by less than 0.2%. At fixed electron spot size, the largest resolvable separation scales as the inverse square of normalized emittance; subnanometer bunches also produce a mode-locked train with 13.9 as spacing. This two-coordinate programmability enables phase-stepped multicolor measurements and offers routes to hard-X-ray Ramsey interferometry, coherent control of core and nuclear excitations, and attosecond nonlinear spectroscopy.
item.dc:creator: Hao Zhang, Ji Qiang, Shukui Zhang, Sergio Carbajo
